basis: Antecubital skin webbing with restricted elbow extension and radioulnar joint maldevelopment defines the syndrome.
Degeneration of the peripheral retina.
Malignant osteoid-producing tumor arising in bone; pulmonary metastasis is not assumed from its potential to spread.
Mitochondrial disorder; severe CNS dysfunction, hearing impairment and microcytic anemia each reported in 1/1 patient. Muscle DNA depletion alone does not establish myopathy.
Microcephaly, intellectual disability, ataxia and spasticity define neurologic involvement; hyperopia reported in 1/1 patient. Immunodeficiency explicitly absent.
Clonal plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal light/heavy-chain deposits; renal deposition with proteinuria or impaired function occurs in nearly all patients.
Fungal infection directly inflames and damages skeletal muscle.
5p deletion spectrum, including cri-du-chat, predominantly causes neurodevelopmental impairment; additional organ malformations vary with deletion extent.
Malignancy originating in minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Severe neurodevelopmental disability with microcephaly and absent language; hearing impairment reported in 2/2 patients.
Inherited predisposition specifically targets cutaneous melanoma; this label does not imply an existing melanoma or damage to other organs.
Nephrocalcinosis, conductive hearing loss and cleft palate/annular pancreas each occur in 30-79%. Frequent ocular and joint abnormalities omitted under the four-axis cap.
Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen; cutaneous hemorrhagic lesions and gingival breakdown each affect roughly 30% or more. Anemia is often secondary.
Brain malformations, cerebellar degeneration and seizures; hearing impairment in 2/2 assessed and retinopathy in 1/1 assessed, with small denominators.
Intellectual disability, speech impairment and abnormal neurologic development define the syndrome. Hearing loss and other functional organ defects occur in only 5-29%.
Inherited osteonecrosis directly destroys the femoral head; local ischemia does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Benign mesenchymal soft-tissue neoplasm; renal and pulmonary locations are subtype-specific and are not assigned across this umbrella.
Congenital spinal dysraphism with an epithelial dermal tract extending into the intrathecal space. Meningitis is a risk rather than established infection.
Ulceration directly damages the duodenal wall; an infectious cause is not specified.
VIP-secreting pancreatic endocrine tumor with defining intestinal secretory dysfunction and electrolyte disturbance. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.
Congenital herniation of meninges through a defining vertebral or cranial bone defect.
Renal tubulopathy, dilated cardiomyopathy and defining electrolyte/acid-base abnormalities. Pulmonary edema is secondary; hepatic calcification lacks demonstrated functional damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and named ocular anomalies define the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 6/8 assessed patients (75%).
Mycobacterial infection defined by persistent skin lesions and pronounced peripheral nerve damage.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the larynx; myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
